set.body:
THE CROSS-SPACE BRIDGE IS DOCUMENTED, BUILDABLE, INTERNALLY SUPPORTED, AND UNREACHABLE FROM THE PUBLIC API.

This inverts the pattern of the last four findings. Those were working capabilities the documentation hides. This is a capability the documentation SHOWS and the exported surface does not provide.

WHAT WORKS. measurement_bridge() builds a valid object across two different native domains:

  subject A native domain   7 features
  subject B native domain   9 features
  common measurement space  4 dimensions

  bridge built                     effect_measurement_bridge
  left_leg 4x7, right_leg 4x9      correct factorized shape
  reverse_bridge involution        identical(reverse(reverse(x)), x) -> TRUE

So the constructor is sound and the algebraic property the vignette asserts at introduction.Rmd:273 holds.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST. I scanned all 80 exported functions for any parameter matching bridge, common_space or leg. Exactly TWO match:

  measurement_bridge(left_leg, right_leg, left_domain, right_domain, common_space, provenance)
  reverse_bridge(bridge)

One creates a bridge. One reverses a bridge. NOTHING CONSUMES ONE. measurement_form has no bridge parameter - passing one gives 'unused argument'. plan_geometry, geometry, measurement_components and reconstruct_evidence have none either.

I checked the one plausible candidate before filing. measurement_form has a route argument, which could have been the slot. It is not: its default is c('auto','forward_k','pull_h','factorized_h','scalar_stack','multivariate_blocks'), a lowering-strategy selector. Passing a bridge gives "'arg' must be NULL or a character vector".

THE ENGINE SUPPORTS IT. R/evidence-task.R:60 defines

  .closed_neural_boundary(bridge, left_relation, right_relation)

which validates a measurement bridge and produces a closure with closure_kind = 'bridge', signature-tracked at line 85, and validated at lines 240-246 where a closed neural boundary requires one bridge or query closure. So the internal machinery is built, wired and checked. It is simply not exported, and no exported function reaches it.

WHY THIS MATTERS. introduction.Rmd devotes an entire section - 'Require a bridge between neural spaces', lines 248 to 281 - to bridges. It explains why relations with different neural feature identities cannot be multiplied, builds a bridge, verifies its dimensions and involution in a hidden chunk, and explains the factorization t(left_leg) %*% right_leg. Then the section ENDS. The bridge is never used for anything, in the vignette or anywhere else, because it cannot be.

Cross-subject and cross-space analysis is the capability this section advertises. It is also, for many readers, the reason to be interested at all - README explicitly scopes out learning an alignment and group inference, which makes the FIXED bridge the package's entire cross-space story. A reader who follows that section to its end has a validated bridge object in hand and no call to pass it to.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING. I have not established whether the internal path works correctly, only that it exists and is validated. It is possible the export was deliberately withheld pending verification - which would be consistent with the 0.1 stance of not exporting what has no executable, scale-qualified path, stated at introduction.Rmd:243-246 for reduction pipelines.

WHAT TO DO, either is defensible but the current state is not:
  1. export an entry point that accepts a bridge, so the documented section terminates in a
     usable call
  2. or say plainly in the vignette that bridges are constructed and validated in 0.1 but not
     yet consumable, as the package already does for correlation, ranking and Fisher edge
     pipelines at introduction.Rmd:243-246

The package has a precedent for the honest version of option 2 and does not apply it here.
set.title: The cross-space bridge is documented and buildable but no exported function consumes it
